title: Collin S
content: The light was everything and it was more than I could ever describe. It felt like pure love and total understanding all at once. I wasn't scared at all. It was the most peaceful I have ever felt. I heard a voice, but it wasn't a sound you hear with your ears. It was more like a thought placed directly in my mind. It asked me if I was ready to go, and I said I didn't know. It told me it wasn't my time. Suddenly, I was being pulled back, and it felt incredibly fast. The next thing I knew, I heard a loud beeping noise and I was back in my body in the hospital room. The feeling of that peace has stayed with me ever since. I used to be so afraid, but not anymore. I know there's nothing to fear.

elements.At the time of your experience, was ther: Yes, Suicide attempt, Other (briefly specify), As far as I know I was dead (no physically detectable life presence) for an undetermined amount of time.
elements.Did you feel separated from your body?: I clearly left my body and existed outside it
elements.How did your highest level of consciousn: More consciousness and alertness than normal, I had a sense of contentedness, I guess. I was at the same time dumbfounded by what I was seeing, I remembered what had just happened with the suicide attempt, but it was like I was observing everything, and I knew I was supposed to observe it, and I was in the state that I was supposed to be in. I'm not sure if I'm communicating that well enough or not.
elements.At what time during the experience were: At the conclusion of the "volume dial" description of my experience, I was completely aware, alert, and fully myself for the remainder of the experience.
elements.Please compare your vision during the ex: It is hard to express exactly how different my level of vision or hearing was. I'm not sure if it was a result of my mind trying to process the fact that I still existed, maybe racing a little bit, or not. As I have previously stated, I can remember the entire experience in vivid detail as though it happened only moments ago, and though I have a better than decent memory, experiences in my life being recalled so vividly are very limited, if not singular in this case.
elements.Please compare your hearing during the e: I would say the same as above, though I do not actually recall hearing any specific sounds during the entirety of the experience. This is not to say that sound was not present, just that nothing of importance surfaces. For example, there may have been wind or a breeze, but I do not recall it. Nothing of any significance transpired in regards to sound during the experience.
elements.Did you pass into or through a tunnel?: Uncertain, Some might describe the light that I saw, which eventually grew to encompass me, as a tunnel. I would not. It was more like a point of light that, as I said, grew to encompass me. Or I was moved toward it, or it toward me, at an incredible speed. I cannot be sure exactly.
elements.Did you encounter or become aware of any: Yes, The man standing before me, as described in my account of the NDE. I do not know if he is supposed to be included. I do not know if he was deceased or alive, but he seemed to be living at the time, was animated, etc., though I do not know what it would mean to be alive or dead in a place such as that.
elements.Did you see, or feel surrounded by, a br: A light clearly of mystical or other-worldly origin
elements.Did you see an unearthly light?: Yes, I am not sure if I would necessarily describe the light as unearthly in and of itself, but the properties of its growth and how it encompassed me were like nothing I have ever experienced before or since. Another thing I believe I left out of the description of the experience itself in this iteration is that everything in the place with the mist had a blue hue to it. I am not sure if it was the color of the light permeating through and over everything, or if everything was colored blue, but I assume it was the former. The light emanating from where my body should have been was definitely of an unearthly tone or property.
elements.Did you seem to enter some other, uneart: A clearly mystical or unearthly realm, As described in my original account of the experience: the void, the place with the mist and the previously undescribed blue light or blue hue. A place seemingly made of mist, with an assumedly blue-colored light illuminating and coloring everything in a pale blue hue, and before that a seemingly endless expanse of nothingness, a complete and utter void, until the appearance or discovery of the pixel of light. I would also include the transitional state between the two aforementioned places.
elements.What emotions did you feel during the ex: Calm, wonder, awe, contentedness, dumbfoundedness, and possibly a sense of purpose, in that I was doing what I was supposed to do as described previously.
elements.Did you feel a sense of harmony or unity: I felt no longer in conflict with nature
elements.Did you come to a border or point of no: I came to a barrier that I was not permitted to cross; or was sent back against my will, I was not in control of the process of regaining my consciousness or awakening on my bedroom floor. I was either being pushed, guided, or shown; I did not freely make my own way through this process. When the man turned and looked at me and I awoke on the floor, there was no whoosh or transition at all. One moment I was in the place with the mist, and then instantly I was not; I was on my bedroom floor waking up.
elements.What was your religion prior to your exp: Unaffiliated- Agnostic, While technically agnostic, I had convinced myself through what I considered logical means that there was nothing after this life. I despaired over it for a long time.
elements.Have your religious practices changed si: Yes, Because some of the aspects of what I saw align with Gnostic thought or description of certain realms, as I've come to understand them. Specifically the description of the planes or realms called the repentance and the sojourn.
elements.What is your religion now?: Other or several faiths, Currently leaning more toward Gnostic (Sethian) but still largely agnostic.
elements.Did your experience include features con: Content that was entirely not consistent with the beliefs you had at the time of your experience, I wanted very badly for life to have meaning, to make sense, and for existence to continue after death. But I had, through various means, convinced myself that nothing existed after death. I despaired over it for a long time, even after my experience, as I had for a while come to doubt that it was real, even though it seemed very real at the time. I had allowed creeping doubt about brain death to enter my mind. What I encountered in my experience did not align with anything I believed at the time, or had previously believed, or had any image of in my own mind.
elements.Did you have a change in your values and: Yes, I hope to do as little harm as I can before leaving this place. I cannot say that before I hoped to do harm, but I definitely did not care as much, and there were also definitely instances before where I wanted to harm certain people for perceived injustices against me.
elements.Did you seem to encounter a mystical bei: I encountered a definite being, or a voice clearly of mystical or unearthly origin, The man that I encountered did not exhibit an unearthly appearance or characteristics, other than that he appeared in a place of unearthly description. He did not levitate, was not shining with light, and was not ghostly. Nothing of the sort. But I included him anyway because of the circumstances under which he was present.
elements.During your experience, did you gain inf: Yes, All of the information described previously led me to believe that existence does not end when our physical form dies here in the material world. I did not receive specific directed information such as "This is the afterlife." I came to be myself again through the aforementioned process and arrived in multiple places: the void and the mist.
elements.Have your relationships changed specific: Yes, I try to be kinder, though I also generally try to avoid people, but the latter is not because of my experience with my NDE.
elements.Was the experience difficult to express: Uncertain, Some parts seem like the words I'm using are lacking in describing exactly what the experience was like. An example is my emotional state during the experience, feeling "dumbfounded" or having a sense of awe but simultaneously feeling calm or content.
elements.How accurately do you remember the exper: I remember the experience more accurately than other life events that occurred around the time of the experience, I can remember almost every detail of the experience vividly, more vividly than anything else I can think of that transpired at the time of the event, prior to it, or after it, with the exception of normal things like what I was doing ten seconds ago. Obviously, all I can remember is what I remember. If there are aspects of the experience that I forgot, I would not know.
elements.Are there one or several parts of your e: The entire experience is meaningful. It is probably the most significant spiritual experience I have ever had, and I cherish it.
elements.Did you have any knowledge of near death: Yes, I knew of the term NDE and had read about others' experiences or seen information about them, for example, on television shows, in a very limited capacity. As far as I know, nothing I had heard or read about affected me or the way I experienced what happened after leaving the material world.
elements.What did you believe about the reality o: Experience was definitely real, I was convinced that it was a real, lived experience. As to why, because it seemed like it was. I was as myself as I am now typing this out during the experience, and it seemed very solid before me. The experience was directed, not distorted or foggy in the mental sense of the word.
elements.What do you believe about the reality of: Experience was definitely real, Exactly as stated above, and now also because of how vividly I can recall it.
elements.Did the questions asked and information: Yes, They do. I'm unsure how to answer this, given my response.
